newsitem.title: USA: Dole faults Clinton on Iraq "pinpricks". [CORRECTED 13:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dole faults Clinton on Iraq "pinpricks". [CORRECTED 13:50 GMT]

text.p: Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole criticised President Bill Clinton in remarks aired Monday for "pinpricks" against Iraq rather than tougher punishment for aggressive behaviour.

Dole, in an interview on the ABC "Good Morning America" (corrects) programme taped Sunday, faulted Clinton for failing to line up more international support for U.S. policy aimed at boxing in President Saddam Hussein and failing to consult Congress more.
"But if you're going to do something, you're going to inflict enough punishment (so) you don't have to keep going back with the pinpricks each time," he said.

President Clinton ordered the firing of 44 cruise missiles at air defence targets in southern Iraq in back-to-back strikes this month to punish Saddam for sending troops into a Western-protected enclave in northern Iraq to back a faction in inter-Kurdish fighting.
Dole said Iraq apparently would be able to repair radars damaged in the U.S. raids in three days and ridiculed the use of million-dollar missiles to attack what he said were $60,000 radars.
"That's not very good economics," he said, adding that he had commented very little about Iraq for fear of appearing to be playing politics where U.S. national security was concerned.

"And of course, he shouldn't play politics either," Dole said. Pressed on whether he thought Clinton had been playing politics with Iraq policy, Dole said: "I may think a lot of things, but I don't talk about it."
